note: Let x=a_1 and y=a_2 as nonzero residue classes modulo p. Successive recurrence values, when admissible, are a_3=(1+y)/x, a_4=(1+x+y)/(xy), a_5=(1+x)/y, a_6=x, a_7=y. Thus the only exclusions on (x,y) are x=-1, y=-1, x+y+1=0. The first two leave (p-2)^2 pairs; among them the last equation has p-2 solutions, one for each x nonzero and not -1. Hence F(p)=(p-2)(p-3), which is 0 or 2 mod 5 because p mod 5 is 1,2,3,4.
